mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate trend consistently reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 0.5% in a sustained manner, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. The effect is only significant when both conditions are met.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market expansion (HOUST above 1500 thousand units), increased residential construction activity signals strong consumer confidence and higher disposable income, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1500.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market that increases wage pressures and corporate profit margins, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is declining.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 (index 2017=100), it signals a contraction in manufacturing and services output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and decline in real GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates stagflationary pressures that reduce corporate profit margins and investor confidence, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The effect is only significant when both conditions are met.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises and GDPC1 declines simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of strong industrial output (INDPRO above 105), robust manufacturing activity signals healthy corporate earnings and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 105.
